data.name: Maadini
data.gender_notes: Maadini is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is obedient and devoted to Allah. Derived from the Arabic root 'aa-da-na', meaning 'to serve'. In Islamic tradition, this name symbolizes devotion, obedience, and submission to Allah. The name Maadini carries the meaning “A servant of Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Maadini usually hope their child will grow to embody a servant of allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Serving and obeying Allah with utmost devotion and faith.
data.etymology: Maadini belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “A servant of Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maadini total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Maadini" emphasizes the importance of serving and obeying Allah in Islamic culture. It encourages individuals to lead pious lives and contribute to their community while following divine guidance.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name "Maadini" conveys the idea of submitted servitude to the Divine. It reminds the bearer of their role as Allah's servant, fostering continual devotion and a strong spiritual connection. This ultimately leads to the attainment of a virtuous and God-recognizing existence.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh al-Buldan. Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrates the conquest of Egypt by the Muslim Arabs under the command of Amr ibn al-As in 639-641 AD. Maadini is mentioned as a village in the region of Fayyum.
historical_references.context: The Conquest of Egypt by Muslim Arabs

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi, Al-Khitat al-Khawarizmiyah. Maadini is mentioned as an agricultural center in the region of Fayyum, Egypt, during the Fatimid Caliphate (969-1171 AD).

In the modern context, this name is seen on various educational platforms that cater to Islamic education. Google Classroom Maadini is another platform where teachers can create virtual classrooms and distribute Islamic educational content. Lastly, Duolingo Maadini, a language-learning platform, offers courses on Arabic and other Islamic languages, contributing to the digital learning and e-learning trends in Islamic education.
